_comment: The merge bar for `develop`, as a contract this repository can check.
GitHub enforces it; this file states what enforcement is supposed to look
like, and `pnpm ci:verify-merge-bar` compares the two. Neither is the
source of truth on its own: GitHub decides what actually happens, and this
decides whether that is what anybody agreed to.
It is expressed as a ruleset rather than as classic branch protection for
one measured reason: the workflow-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN gets 403 on
that, checking this from CI would need a stored token with
administration: read, which would be the first long-lived credential this
Classic branch protection is still in force alongside it. Both apply and
GitHub takes the most restrictive result, so this adds a second enforcement
rather than replacing one — and removing the classic rules is a separate
required_status_checks: No approval from a listed account
